refutes.statement: Reduction (a) with Theorem Z's potential at the best key: some key (g, x) has every maximum of (r', Lambda') completable (so a rule choosing the key, or a tie-break after (r', Lambda'), rescues a black-box use of Theorem Z). Refuted: at every key (7, 0), (7, 1), (7, 2) the maximum of (r', Lambda') is unique, has t = 1, and is not completable.

Reduction (c), one role swap, two-level rule: take a non-completable (r', Lambda')-maximum at a key (g, x) and a terminal z of it (a free agent needing g; (g, z) is a key); then every (r', Lambda')-maximum at (g, z) is completable. Refuted (all 384 failures with n <= 3 are in this core; every non-completable (r', Lambda')-maximum here has two terminals, and their keys fail too).

Conjecture GLOB without t: every maximum over the configurations of all keys of (r', Lambda') (Theorem Z's potential, levels over U_y) is completable. (k4/c4min_reduce.md §5 lists this variant as failing on 123,180 profiles with n <= 3, counter FAIL_glob_r,lamU, without naming an instance.)
refutes.derived_how: Implied by the source's per-key statement (a global maximum is a maximum at its own key); confirmed here with the branch's k4/red_lib.py: 3 global maxima of (r', Lambda'), 0 completable.

refutes.statement: #50's Psi = (r, Lambda) over all keys (Lambda over R_i including the frozen agent's level): some Psi-maximum is completable. (k4/c4min_reduce.md §5.1: 'In 128 (all in the core of H★) none is, so Psi cannot be kept there'; the source gives the count, not this profile.)
refutes.derived_how: Confirmed here with k4/red_lib.py: the 3 maxima of (r, Lambda_R) over all keys are the three unique per-key maxima above, none completable.
